text:
Waste Management - Domestic and industrial liquid wastes generated within the Project Area may be handled in a number of environmentally acceptable ways. Depending on the amount of domestic wastes generated, these wastewaters may be treated in a sewage treatment facility, septic tanks or leach fields, or chemically treated and transported from the Project Area. There is a sewer lagoon on the mine site. This facility is maintained, and operated in compliance with applicable regulations. If septic tanks or leach fields are used, they too would be located, constructed, and monitored in compliance with current regulations to insure proper operation and acceptable dispersal of leachate.
Adequate collection sites and disposal plans for industrial liquid wastes, such as excess, contaminated, or finished fuels, lubricants, solvents or other organic liquids, will be made available within the Project Area. Proper safeguards will also be maintained to prevent the dispersal of organic liquids to surface or ground-water resources.
Various forms of solid wastes (including toxic wastes) may be generated within the mining area. Solid wastes which cannot be burned or buried are transported from the area for proper disposal. If a sanitary landfill were to be utilized, careful site selection, proper operation, and control of dispersion of leachage would have to be carried out in compliance with prevailing State and Federal regulations or recommendations.
All potential waste management, as well as water-quality problems, must be addressed in full compliance with all State and Federal regulations.
